solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Island’s monarch receiving international post

indicators.note: whatever is receiving something takes it inside itself, so one word is opened up to hold the rest

blocks.note: a prince is a ruling monarch in a principality
I is the standard abbreviation for international
P is short for post, as in p and p

explanation.surface: A ruler of some island state takes delivery of overseas mail.
explanation.walkthrough: The two single letters go in together, I then P, between the C and E of the ruler. The island is the smaller half of São Tomé and Príncipe off West Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Príncipe is a volcanic island in the Gulf of Guinea, part of a small African nation.

clue.text: Go west with old man in America on vacation

blocks.note: pop is American for father, an old man
someone off work is away on holiday

explanation.surface: Heading to the West Coast with Dad on an American holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go west' sounds like a road trip, but it is an idiom for dying, and so is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal euphemisms for dying, so going west and popping off mean the same.

clue.text: Think up plan to get Boris’s address shortened

indicators.note: something shortened has been cut down, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: an idea is a plan or scheme
Boris Johnson, then Prime Minister, lived at Number Ten Downing Street

explanation.surface: Someone devises a scheme to cut short a Boris Johnson speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' suggests a speech, but it is where Boris lived: the Prime Minister's home is 10 Downing Street, so the number is written as a word and loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To ideate is to form an idea or concept in the mind, so it means to invent mentally.

clue.text: Nowadays might one say google “throw a fight”

blocks.note: to cast is to throw
taken as written
a bout is a boxing or wrestling match

explanation.surface: A wry remark that people now search the internet to learn how to fix a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw a fight' reads as one phrase about cheating in boxing, but it splits into three pieces; the opening words say we now google where once we'd have cast about.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast about is to search around for something, which is what googling for information does today.

clue.text: One fed in the street by people with bangers?

definitions.text: One fed in the street by people with bangers?

blocks.clueFragment: One fed in the street by people with bangers?
blocks.note: surface reading: a stray animal given sausages by passers-by at a street party

blocks.clueFragment: One fed in the street by people with bangers?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a coin-operated roadside device that motorists, even ones with old wrecks, feed with money

explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for both a sausage and a decrepit old car; feeding is putting coins in a slot.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivers feed coins into a roadside machine to pay for leaving their car, old or new, at the kerb.

clue.text: Johnson now possibly showing resistance after blunder

indicators.note: placing one element after another simply means writing them in sequence, the second following the first

blocks.note: a gaffe is an embarrassing blunder
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson, then Prime Minister, is shown fighting back after yet another of his famous blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: When the puzzle appeared Boris Johnson was Prime Minister, so 'now' he was the boss of the country; gaffer is British slang for a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaffer is informal British for the person in charge, so a sitting prime minister could be called that.

clue.text: Can’t Stand Losing You is 60 mins by a redub’s end

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept
to lose something is to be left without it, so a letter is taken away
by means beside or next to, so the pieces are set side by side

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of the word
sixty minutes make an hour
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: A quiz fact: The Police hit Can't Stand Losing You runs to an hour on some re-recording.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make it look like the song title by The Police, but only the first two words define; the rest is wordplay, with the hour dropping its U.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor something is to loathe it, so if you abhor it you find it unbearable.

clue.text: Odd-job man about to enter big old corporation

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: big and fat are synonyms for large
C is short for circa, Latin for about
O is the abbreviation for old
corporation is old jocular slang for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: A handyman is about to start work at a large, long-established company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' suggests a business, but it is an old joke word for a fat stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum is a servant or employee who does all kinds of jobs, a general handyman.

clue.text: Matters which have remained unsettled in Red issue

indicators.note: something unsettled is disturbed and out of place, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the eight letters taken as printed

explanation.surface: Unresolved business at a left-wing party or Manchester United, the Reds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matters' looks like the abstract noun for issues, but it means physical stuff that is left over.
explanation.definitionFit: Residues are substances left over after a process, so they are material that stays behind.

clue.text: Running round meadows is unadulterated joy

indicators.note: something running round an object encircles it, so one word wraps around another

blocks.note: unadulterated means pure, unmixed
leas are meadows, a poetic and crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Racing about in the fields is sheer delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' looks like the activity in the meadows, but with 'round' it tells you the outer word goes around the inner one, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure and joy are near synonyms for a feeling of happiness or delight.

clue.text: European people, I’m told, can become vets

indicators.note: what someone is told is heard rather than read, so the sound matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: people from the Czech Republic, a European country

explanation.surface: A claim that some Europeans are able to retrain as veterinary surgeons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vets' looks like a noun for animal doctors but is a verb here: to vet something is to examine it.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet a candidate or document is to inspect it carefully, which is what checking means.

clue.text: Flashy power shower with some cracks in it?

definitions.text: Flashy power shower with some cracks in it?

blocks.clueFragment: Flashy power shower with some cracks in it?
blocks.note: surface reading: a showy, high-pressure bathroom shower with a cracked tray or tiles

blocks.clueFragment: Flashy power shower with some cracks in it?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a powerful burst of rain that comes with lightning flashes and cracks of noise from the sky

explanation.walkthrough: A power shower is a strong electric shower in British bathrooms; here every word turns to weather, with flashes of lightning and claps of the noise that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent storm brings heavy rain, lightning flashes and loud cracking claps from the sky.

clue.text: Interrupting stupid answer, wife shows judgement

indicators.note: to interrupt something is to break into the middle of it, so one letter goes inside the others

blocks.note: fat can mean dull or stupid, as in fat-headed
A is the usual abbreviation for answer
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A wife butts in on a foolish reply and makes her opinion known.
explanation.walkthrough: The wife's letter breaks into the pair formed by the first two pieces, landing just before the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatwa is a formal legal ruling issued by an Islamic scholar, so it is a judgement.

clue.text: Writer one associates with Notts Forest

indicators.note: to associate with something is to join up alongside it, so the parts are set side by side

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
the famous forest of Nottinghamshire, home of Robin Hood

explanation.surface: An author says which football club he follows: Nottingham Forest.
explanation.walkthrough: Notts Forest is the football club Nottingham Forest, but read literally it is the forest of Nottinghamshire (Notts), which is Sherwood.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Isherwood was an English novelist, author of Goodbye to Berlin and A Single Man.

clue.text: Is enough gold being newly-found in digs?

indicators.note: something newly found is set out afresh, so these letters come in a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: the twelve letters taken as printed

explanation.surface: Prospectors wonder whether enough gold is turning up at their excavation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digs' suggests archaeology or mining to go with the gold, but it is British slang for rented rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Digs is informal British for lodgings, a rented room or rooms in someone's house.

clue.text: A cause of hot gusts blowing through Barnet?

definitions.text: A cause of hot gusts blowing through Barnet?

blocks.clueFragment: A cause of hot gusts blowing through Barnet?
blocks.note: surface reading: a heatwave or warm wind sweeping across the north London borough of Barnet

blocks.clueFragment: A cause of hot gusts blowing through Barnet?
blocks.note: setter's reading: Barnet is rhyming slang for the hair on your head, so this is the gadget that blows warm air through it

explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is a London borough, but Cockney rhyming slang 'Barnet Fair' means hair; Barnet is also a football club, nicely recalling Alex Ferguson's 'hairdryer treatment'.
explanation.definitionFit: The handheld appliance blows a stream of heated air across wet hair to dry it.

clue.text: Good and bad papers featuring rowdy man in Top Gear

indicators.note: a programme featuring someone has them inside it, so one piece sits within the others

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
rags are low-quality newspapers
a lad is a boisterous young man, as in laddish

explanation.surface: The press, good and bad, report on a loudmouth presenter of the TV motoring show Top Gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Top Gear is a BBC car programme whose presenters made tabloid headlines, but here it means one's best clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags are one's smartest clothes for a special occasion, so they are the finest outfit.

clue.text: Clothing in refuse container mostly rubbish

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: a skip is a large open bin for building waste
pants is British slang for rubbish, as in 'that film was pants'

explanation.surface: Someone finds garments in a waste bin, most of them junk.
explanation.walkthrough: A skip is a British builders' rubbish container, and pants is British slang for worthless; the container loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ski pants are close-fitting trousers worn for skiing, an item of clothing.

clue.text: What Satanists do with great intensity

blocks.note: first meaning: devil-worshippers are fond of Satan
second meaning: an idiom for doing something furiously hard

explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads the phrase literally, with 'like' as a verb meaning to be fond of; the second is the everyday idiom, as in 'ran like the devil'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes acting with furious energy, as in working or running extremely hard and fast.

clue.text: Red fog seen covering area close to Cairo

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept
to cover something is to wrap around it, so one word encloses the rest

blocks.note: mist is a light fog
A is the abbreviation for area
the final letter of the city

explanation.surface: A reddish haze is spotted over a district on the edge of Cairo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' looks like a colour for the fog, but it is the political sense, a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: A Maoist is a follower of Mao Zedong's communism, and Red is a common label for communists.

clue.text: Dreadful ordeal in a border city

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a terrible state, so these letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: the six letters taken as printed

explanation.surface: Someone endures a terrible experience in a frontier town.
explanation.walkthrough: Laredo is in Texas on the Rio Grande, facing Nuevo Laredo across the Mexican border.
explanation.definitionFit: Laredo sits on the US-Mexico frontier, one of the busiest crossing points between the countries.

clue.text: Order step to change some Home Office staff?

indicators.note: to change something is to alter it, so the letters are rearranged into a new word

blocks.note: the nine letters taken as printed

explanation.surface: A ministry instructs its officials to take a different course of action.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Office is the UK government department responsible for immigration; the question mark admits that only some of its staff fit the description.
explanation.definitionFit: Officials who remove people from the country are deporters, and that removal is a Home Office function.

clue.text: Poet’s line nicked by Republican president

indicators.note: whatever is nicked is taken and pocketed, so one letter is held inside the others

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
Ike was the nickname of President Dwight Eisenhower
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A poet complains that a Republican president plagiarised one of his lines.
explanation.walkthrough: Eisenhower was himself a Republican, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainer Maria Rilke was a Bohemian-Austrian writer of verse, author of the Duino Elegies.

clue.text: Play doctor and primarily nurses in the morning

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only an opening letter is kept
to nurse is to hold close and cradle, so one part holds another inside it

blocks.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
the opening letter of the little word
AM, ante meridiem, marks times in the morning

explanation.surface: Children playing doctors and nurses before lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play doctor' looks like a game, but 'Play' alone is the definition; the first three letters together cradle the morning's two between their last pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play written for performance on stage, radio or television.

clue.text: Cancels yearbooks after the fifth fails to show

indicators.text: after the fifth fails to show
indicators.note: a letter that fails to show is missing, and this names exactly which position goes

blocks.note: annuals are books published once a year

explanation.surface: A school scraps its yearbooks after the fifth year doesn't turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: The fifth letter of the yearbooks, an A, is the one that disappears.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul something is to declare it void, which is to cancel it officially.

clue.text: Very aggressive type of delivery yob lined up

indicators.note: things that are up are in turmoil or disorder, as in 'what's up?', so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the eight letters taken as printed

explanation.surface: A thug queues up to deliver something nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler's throw is a delivery; bodyline was the England tactic of bowling fast at the batsman's body in the 1932-33 Ashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Bodyline bowling aimed at the batsman's body to intimidate, notoriously hostile cricket tactics.

clue.text: It is located east of southern American county

indicators.note: in an across answer east is to the right, so this piece is written after the others

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
US for American, as in US citizen
it is a coy word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A geography note: some place lies to the east of a southern US county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like a pronoun for the place, but it is the old slang for sex appeal. Sussex is a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Sussex is a historic English county, now split into East and West Sussex.

clue.text: Cordial head of office following a horse racing event

indicators.note: the head of anything is its top or front, so only the opening letter is kept
one thing following another comes after it in the line, so the order is fixed

blocks.note: taken as written
a mare is a female horse
the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle race
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A friendly office manager turns up after a day at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cordial' looks like an adjective describing the head of office, but it is a noun for a sweet liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaretto is an almond-flavoured Italian liqueur, and a cordial can be a sweet alcoholic liqueur.
